purpose: Zolmitriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with a migraine. It is not used to prevent migraines, only to treat them once they start.
how_it_works: When you get a migraine, certain blood vessels in your brain widen and cause pain. Zolmitriptan works by attaching to specific receptors in your brain that cause those blood vessels to narrow back down. It also helps block pain signals in the brain, which is why it can stop a migraine in its tracks.
common_side_effects: You might feel a tingly, warm, or tight sensation in your face, neck, or chest after taking it. Some people feel a little dizzy, drowsy, or nauseous. You may also notice a dry mouth or a feeling of heaviness or pressure in your body. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not use this medicine if you have heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or a history of stroke. Tell your doctor if you have ever had heart problems or risk factors like smoking or diabetes. Do not take it within 24 hours of other triptan medicines or ergotamine-type drugs. If you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, or a very severe headache, seek emergency help right away. Let your doctor know about all other medicines you take, especially antidepressants, as dangerous interactions can occur.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 2.5 mg taken by mouth at the first sign of a migraine. If the migraine comes back after it went away, you can take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first one. Do not take more than 10 mg in any 24-hour period. The dissolving tablet is placed on your tongue and melts without water, which is handy if you feel nauseous.
